ER Echo installer (ER-Echo-Setup.exe) - bundled runtime notices
================================================================

ER-Echo-Setup.exe is a PyInstaller "onedir" build. The folder you extracted contains the
Python program plus the runtime libraries it needs. They are third-party components, not part
of ER Echo's own code:

  Qt 6.12 (QtCore / QtGui / QtWidgets / plugins)
      Copyright (C) The Qt Company Ltd.
      License: GNU Lesser General Public License v3 (LGPL-3.0), no commercial Qt license used.
      https://www.qt.io/licensing/open-source-lgpl-obligations

  PySide6 6.12 and shiboken6 6.12
      Copyright (C) The Qt Company Ltd.
      License: LGPL-3.0 (Qt for Python).
      https://www.qt.io/qt-for-python

  CPython 3.11
      Copyright (c) Python Software Foundation.
      License: Python Software Foundation License 2.0 (PSF-2.0).
      https://docs.python.org/3/license.html

  OpenSSL 3 (libcrypto-3.dll, used by Python's hashlib)
      Copyright (c) The OpenSSL Project.
      License: Apache License 2.0.

  libffi (libffi-8.dll, used by Python's ctypes)
      Copyright (c) 1996-2024 Anthony Green, Red Hat, Inc and others.
      License: MIT (see libffi-LICENSE.txt).

  PyInstaller 6 (bundle loader)
      Copyright (c) 2010-2026 PyInstaller Development Team.
      License: GPL-2.0-or-later with a special exception that explicitly allows building and
      distributing non-free/closed-source programs (see PyInstaller-COPYING.txt).

  Microsoft Visual C++ runtime (MSVCP140.dll, VCRUNTIME140*.dll)
      Redistributable under the Microsoft Visual Studio license terms.

Full texts are in this LICENSES folder:
  LGPL-3.0.txt, GPL-3.0.txt, PSF-Python-3.11.txt, Apache-2.0.txt,
  libffi-LICENSE.txt, PyInstaller-COPYING.txt

LGPL compliance note
--------------------
Qt and PySide6 are used unmodified and are linked dynamically: the Qt DLLs and the PySide6
extension modules sit next to ER-Echo-Setup.exe inside _internal\, so you can replace them with
your own compatible builds (or delete them and supply them yourself) without recompiling ER
Echo. Nothing in the ER Echo license restricts reverse engineering of these libraries for the
purpose of debugging your modifications. ER Echo's own source is at
https://github.com/Sanvenir/ER-Echo (MIT OR Apache-2.0); it does not include Qt or PySide6 code.

The ER Echo mod itself (er_echo.dll) is NOT part of the Qt/PySide6 work: it is a separate
component, embedded as data, built in Rust on fromsoftware-rs under its own NON-AI license (see
THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt §2).
